questionText: Shall the Township Committee of the Township of West Amwell amend Chapter 35, Section 35-3 of the Township Code, entitled “Funding,” to provide that the Municipal Open Space, Farmland and Recreation and Historic Preservation Trust Fund shall be funded by an annual tax levy in an amount up to, but not exceeding, $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation, rather than requiring the annual levy to be set at $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation?
officialStatement: A “Yes” vote authorizes the Township Committee to amend Section 35-3 of the Township Code so that the annual dedicated levy for the Municipal Open Space, Farmland and Recreation and Historic Preservation Trust Fund may be set each year in an amount up to, but not exceeding, $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation. The current ordinance provides for an annual levy of exactly $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation. Approval of this question would not increase the maximum authorized open space levy. Instead, it would allow the Township Committee to levy less than $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation in a particular year if the Township Committee determines that a lower levy is appropriate. Funds raised by the levy would continue to be dedicated to the purposes authorized for the Municipal Open Space, Farmland and Recreation and Historic Preservation Trust Fund, including open space, recreation, farmland preservation, historic preservation, and related purposes authorized by law. A “No” vote means Section 35-3 would remain unchanged, and the ordinance would continue to provide for an annual levy of $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation.

The State debt service aid percentage is equal to 40% of the annual debt service due with respect to the final eligible costs of the projects. Do you approve this Bond Proposal Question?

questionText: Shall the Board of Education of the Bloomsbury School District be permitted to join the North Hunterdon-Voorhees Regional High School District as a constituent member with the tax apportionment formula to remain 100% on each municipality’s equalized valuation allocated to the regional district as provided by state law and with the membership of the North Hunterdon- Vorhees Regional Board of Education to be expanded to 13 members with such membership to be apportioned utilizing the same methodology currently utilized by the North Hunterdon-Voorhees Regional Board of Education.
officialStatement: Beginning with the 2025-26 school year, students from Bloomsbury began attending North Hunterdon High School through a sending-receiving (contractual) relationship. Regardless of whether this referendum passes, Bloomsbury students will continue to attend North Hunterdon High School. If this referendum passes, Bloomsbury will become a constituent member of the North Hunterdon-Voorhees Regional High School District. As a constituent member, Bloomsbury residents will gain voting representation on the Regional Board of Education, and Bloomsbury’s share of the regional district’s costs will be allocated based on equalized property valuation, consistent with the Regional District’s current and long-standing practice and state law. The Regional Board of Education will expand from 12 to 13 members, with seats apportioned based on census population data and updated following each decennial census. Based on the 2020 Census, the initial seat allocation would be as follows: • Bethlehem Township and Hampton Borough: 1 representative (elected at-large) • Union Township and Bloomsbury: 2 representatives (elected at-large) • Califon Borough and Tewksbury Township: 2 representatives (elected at-large) • Clinton Township and Lebanon Borough: 4 representatives (elected at-large) • High Bridge Borough and Lebanon Township: 2 representatives (elected at-large) • Town of Clinton, Franklin Township, and Glen Gardner Borough: 2 representatives (elected at-large) If this referendum does not pass, Bloomsbury students will continue to attend North Hunterdon High School under the existing sending-receiving relationship. However, Bloomsbury would not become a constituent member of the regional district, would not have voting representation on the Regional Board of Education, unless and until it sends a sufficient percentage of students to meet the statutory threshold, and would continue to pay tuition under the terms of the sending- receiving agreement rather than contributing through the regional tax apportionment formula.
